plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 creating texts with relevant, sequenced ideas and a structure for topic, purpose and audience; VC2E5LA02 using authoritative sources; VC2E5LE02 opinions on The Last Bear
plan.shape: model a plan, test audience fit, then plan: students see a full plan, judge reasons by who reads them, then plan their own big piece and conference with the teacher, because a strong plan is what makes the next three drafting sessions flow
plan.criticalFeature: the audience decides which reasons and which words will work
decisionPoints: the choice check: the reason that convinces this audience
the plan conference and the exit board
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. The plan puts all three in order for one reader.
plan.catchUp: Missed Weeks 1-3? Give the planner and the model plan. They choose question A, B or C from the Week 1 Issue Card Scaffold and use the Arctic Fact Cards.

studentTools: Arctic Fact Cards and Power Word Bank from Week 2
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: The big piece structure: introduction, body 1, body 2, answer back, conclusion
A conference list: names ticked when each plan is checked

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: match form to reader, choose reasons for a reader, then plan your big piece.
resources.title: Choose Your Fight
resources.subtitle: Plan it for ONE reader. Strongest reason last.

example.answer: an opinion article in the newsletter

items.prompt: Choose the best form: letter, opinion article or open letter.

example.prompt: Issue: longer lunch. Reader: the principal.
steps: What does the reader care about?
Put it last if it's strongest

items.prompt: Issue: a school dog park. Reader: parents. Which reason fits best?
options: Kids walk more when the dog comes too.
items.explain: Parents care about their kids' health; the other two are about the writer.

items.prompt: Leo planned this for the council. Find the problem and fix it.
items.answer: Both reasons are about Leo, not the council. Fix: A skate park keeps kids off busy roads.

steps: Three reasons, strongest last, each with proof
The other side and my call to action
example.answer: A zoo director, a letter, three reasons with proof, the other side answered, and one clear action.

rows: The other side says... I answer...
answers: letter, opinion article or open letter
the reason this reader cares about most
The other side says... I answer...

example.answer: Year 3: bears are lonely; they need room to play.

items.prompt: Plan three reasons for a second reader.
answers: a reason this reader cares about
the reason that matters most to them

example.prompt: Director: money and visitors. Year 3: animals and fairness.
steps: Which reader is harder to persuade?
What would you change in your words?
example.answer: The director: I'd use facts and costs, not feelings.

items.answer: A choice, a reason linked to the reader, and specific word changes.

slides.notes: Open the session. One line: this week you write your big piece, and today you choose your fight.

slides.title: For the teacher: the big piece
lines: Structure (modelled and expected): introduction, body 1, body 2, answer back, conclusion.
Flexible: each student chooses issue, reader, form (letter, opinion article, open letter) and reasons.
This week: S1 plan, S2 introduction, S3 body paragraphs, S4 answer back and conclusion.
Week 5: feedback, revise, edit, publish to a real audience.
Unit anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it.
slides.notes: Teacher-facing only. The piece is highly structured by paragraph; students choose the content. Decide the publishing audience this week (another class, the newsletter, a real organisation).
Print the Worksheet for everyone (its last section is the big piece plan, kept beside the draft all week), the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to plan a persuasive piece for a real reader.
successCriteria: I can choose my issue, my reader and my form.
I can plan three reasons with evidence that would convince my reader.
I can plan words and a tone that suit my reader.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Real writers write for real readers. So will you.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: Choosing your issue and reader is where we start.
Planning reasons that convince that reader is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 choosing issue, reader and form is reachable for all; SC2 reasons for that reader is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 tone is the stretch.

slides.title: Same request, different reader
lines: Can I please stay up later? I'll still be ready for school.
Dear Principal, I am writing to ask for a later finish to lunch.
bro pls can u save me a seat

notes.answer: 1 parent, 2 principal, 3 a mate - the words change with the reader
beats: SAY: Three messages. Three different readers.
You can tell who each one is for.
ASK: Which one is written to the principal?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest, 1, 2 or 3... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What gave it away?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: Dear Principal; I am writing; full words, no slang
SAY: Before you write a word of your big piece, you choose your reader.
trap: thinking audience only changes the greeting.
Fix: ask what else changed? Student finds slang, length, reasons.

slides.meaning: The type of text you write: a letter, an article, a speech.
slides.example: To persuade the council, a formal letter is the right form.

notes.answer: the type of text you write
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Form. Say it with me. Form.
SAY: Form is the type of text. A letter, an article, a speech.
You choose the form that will reach your reader.
ASK: To persuade the whole school, which form would you choose?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: an article in the newsletter; a speech at assembly
trap: confusing form with a printed form you fill in.
Fix: say here form means the type of writing.
notes.prep: Three forms on offer this week: letter, opinion article, open letter. Speech comes in Week 6.

slides.title: Watch me plan for one reader

rows: a zoo director - a formal letter
Zoos should stop bringing in new polar bears.
space, heat, and money better spent in the wild
zoos teach kids - but so can cameras
Fund wild polar bear research instead.

notes.answer: issue, reader, form, position, three reasons, the other side, the action
beats: POINT to Reader and form.
SAY: My reader is a zoo director. A director runs a business and loves animals.
POINT to Reasons.
SAY: So my strongest reason is money: better spent in the wild.
That's what a director can actually act on. Strongest goes last.
POINT to Call to action.
SAY: Something a director can do: fund research. Not shut every zoo.
ASK: Why did I save the money reason for last?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: it matters most to the director; end strong
trap: planning reasons that convince the writer, not the reader.
Fix: student writes their reader's name above each reason and checks it.
notes.stretch: Plan a second, different reader and see which reasons change.
notes.help: Copy the plan's shape; fill one row at a time.
notes.prep: The model plan. Critical feature: the audience decides which reasons and words will work.

slides.title: Which form fits the reader?
slides.pivot: ask: where would this reader actually read it?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: why that form?

items.text: Reader: anyone in Australia who might read it
items.say: An open letter is to everyone, published for all to read. Tick or fix.

items.text: Reader: the Minister for the Environment

say: Choose the form that would reach each reader.
trap: choosing the form they like best for every reader.
Fix: ask where would this reader see it? Student re-chooses.
notes.stretch: Name the greeting each form would start with.
notes.help: Letters go to one person or group; articles go to everyone.

slides.title: Which reason would convince THIS reader?
slides.prompt: Issue: our school needs a vegetable garden. Reader: the school council.

options.text: Gardens are fun and I love getting dirty.
options.misconception: a reason that convinces the writer, not the reader

options.text: A garden can supply the canteen and teach science outside.
Every single school already has one.
options.misconception: a sneaky trick; untrue and easy to dismiss

notes.answer: B - it meets what a school council cares about: money and learning
beats: SAY: Think about the reader: a school council. What do they care about?
ASK: Which reason would convince this reader?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: who would A convince?
Less -> list what a council cares about, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Canteen supplies and science. That's what a council can say yes to.
trap: pointing to A because it's honest.
Fix: ask does the council care that you like dirt? Student re-chooses.
notes.prep: Decision point before planning. Under 80% means students write their reader's name at the top of the planner before any reasons.

slides.title: What does this reader care about?
slides.pivot: picture their job: what keeps them up at night?
slides.followUp: cold call one board: so which reason would you lead with?

items.answer: their kids' safety, health and cost
fun, fairness, animals, things they can do

say: Before you plan, know your reader.
Write two things each reader cares about.
trap: writing what the student cares about.
Fix: ask what is their job? Student answers as the reader.
notes.stretch: Write the word you'd avoid with each reader.
notes.help: Think: what does this person spend their day doing?
notes.prep: Guided audience analysis just before planning. SC2.

slides.title: Plan your big piece
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish by planning your big piece for one reader.
slides.frame: My reader cares about ___, so my strongest reason is ___.

notes.answer: a complete planner aimed at one named reader
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Use your issue from Week 1, or a new one you care about more.
It must connect to The Last Bear's big ideas.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CONFERENCE. Two minutes per student, tick the board list.
Check: one reader, three different reasons, a source for each.
ASK: How many rows of your planner are done?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 4 or more by 15 minutes
TIME 22 minutes.
trap: three reasons that are really one reason three ways.
Fix: ask what's different about reason 2? Student swaps one for a fact card.
notes.stretch: Extension: plan for a second reader, then compare.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a partly filled plan, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent planning with teacher conferences. The planner travels with the draft all week. SC1 and SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in a full plan for the big persuasive piece

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Issue: build a bike path to our school. Reader: the local council.
Write one reason that would convince THAT reader.

notes.answer: e.g. fewer cars at drop-off means safer roads and less traffic for residents
beats: SAY: A new issue and reader. Think like the council.
ASK: Write one reason that would convince the council.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: safety, traffic, health, cost - something a council cares about
RECORD who writes a reason about themselves. Conference first tomorrow.
trap: Because I like riding my bike.
Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new issue. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner your reader and why your strongest reason will work on them.

notes.answer: open - listen for a reason linked to what the reader cares about
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How ready is your plan?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down. Conference them first tomorrow.
ASK: Tell your partner your reader and your strongest reason.
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the principal, because it saves teaching time
notes.prep: Self-assessment read beside the exit boards and conference list. SC2.
